title: Sexing young rabbits
subtitle: How to tell bucks from does reliably from four weeks of age.
excerpt: Sexing rabbits accurately before six to eight weeks is difficult and the source of many accidental litters. At four weeks the external genitalia are small but distinguishable. By eight weeks the difference is reliable in most breeds. Here is the technique for examining kits safely and what to look for at each age.
sourceNotes: British Rabbit Council, rabbit husbandry guidance. RWAF (Rabbit Welfare Association and Fund), rabbit care factsheets. Merck Veterinary Manual, rabbit sexing (online edition, 2023).

glossaryTerms.definition: The external genital and anal region of a rabbit, visible on the underside near the tail. Inspection of the vent is the method used to determine sex.

content.text: Correct sexing before eight weeks prevents accidental litters from litter-mates housed together after weaning. Bucks are sexually mature as young as 10 to 12 weeks in some small breeds, well before the point at which most keepers separate them. The
examination takes under a minute per kit and causes no distress when done with a settled animal.
Cup the kit gently in both hands, keeping it close to your body. Young kits stress easily and can injure themselves by kicking if held insecurely.
Turn the kit onto its back in the palm of one hand, supporting its full weight. Keep your movements slow and deliberate.
Use the thumb and index finger of the other hand to apply gentle pressure just above the tail, exposing the vent.

Doe: a slit-shaped opening immediately above the anal opening, with the two structures close together and both appearing as slits. The vulva in a doe looks like a small, elongated opening pointing toward the tail.

Buck: a small rounded or doughnut-shaped opening, positioned further from the anal opening than in the doe. In older bucks (8 weeks+) the prepuce forms a visible circular rim. There may be a slight protrusion in the very young buck, though the testes do not descend until 10 to 12 weeks.

Separate bucks from does and from other bucks by 10 weeks at the latest, regardless of how confident you are in your sexing. Early-developing bucks can father a litter before testicular descent makes them easy to identify. Small breeds mature faster than large breeds: New Zealand Whites and Continental giants can be left together slightly longer than Miniature Rex or Netherlands Dwarfs.
